rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Kalbi, and Ibn Abbas in Atiyya’s transmission take this as Jonah thinking God would not decree punishment for him.
rows.anchor: قول مجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، والكلبي، ورواية عطية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says ظن is actual conjecture here, not knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد الظن بعينه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains that Jonah thought God would not decree the punishment that God had decreed for him.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ظن أن لن نقدر عليه من العقوبة ما قدرنا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says نقدر here has the sense of نقدر, supporting the interpretation as decreeing punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ونقدر بمعنى: نقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb قدر can mean to decree; the author supports this sense with a line describing a camel’s leg being measured.
rows.anchor: ويقال: قدر الله الشيء وقدره، أي: قضاه. والقدر يكون بمعنى التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse of poetry uses قدرت to mean measured or determined, as evidence for قدر meaning decree or measure.
rows.anchor: ومفرهة عنس قدرت لساقها ... فخرت كما تتايع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Zuhri read with a doubled د; Ubayd ibn Umayr and Qatada read the passive with a doubled د. The two forms also occur at 56:60 and 87:3.
rows.anchor: قراءة عمر بن عبد العزيز والزهري (فظن أن لن نقدر عليه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second explanation takes the phrase to mean that Jonah thought God would not confine or constrict him.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني: فظن أن لن يضيق عليه الحبس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the transmission of Ata, Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as meaning God would not punish Jonah.
rows.anchor: قال] (¬5) في رواية عطاء: أن لن نعاقبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Mansur’s transmission, Ibn Abbas says it refers to the affliction that befell Jonah.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية منصور: يعني (¬7) البلاء الذي أصابه

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham takes نقدر as constrict, citing 65:7 and 89:16; God confined Jonah in the whale more severely than any worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: المعنى: فظن أن لن يضيق عليه

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the phrase as God not constricting Jonah, noting that Arabic calls a person’s provision both مقدر and مقتر when it is restricted.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} أي: لن نضيق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God punished Jonah for his indignation and pride, fleeing, and reluctance to pardon his people and accept their repentance, by confining him inside the whale.
rows.anchor: عاقب الله يونس عن حميته وأنفته

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from Awf, says Jonah thought he could defeat or escape his Lord.
rows.anchor: وروى عوف، عن الحسن، أنه (¬10) قال: معناه: فظن أنه يعجز ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects this reading as remote and impermissible for a prophet.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل بعيد، ولا يجوز مثله على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abu al-Haytham says belief that Jonah thought God powerless is disbelief, since Jonah was a messenger.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الهيثم: من اعتقد أن يونس ظن أن لن يقدر الله عليه فهو كافر

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari argues نقدر cannot mean ability: that would make Jonah doubt God’s power, a disbelief from which prophets are protected; only an ignorant reader of Arabic would hold it.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: قوله (أن لن نقدر عليه) لا يجوز أن يكون من القدرة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash adopts the interpretation attributed to al-Hasan: Jonah thought he would escape God.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب الأخفش إلى مثل ما روي عن الحسن، فقال: فظن أن يفوتنا

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim criticizes al-Akhfash for understanding نقدر as ability rather than constriction, saying he knew grammar but not Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حاتم: لم يدر الأخفش ما معنى (نقدر) وذهب إلى القدرة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the wording as an implicit question, “Did he suppose…?” The author rejects this because omitting the interrogative is allowed only by poetic necessity, especially without a contextual cue.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن زيد أنه قال: هذا إستيفاه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and all commentators identify the darknesses as night, sea, and the whale’s belly.
rows.anchor: يعني: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة بطن الحوت. قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d gives the sequence as the first whale’s interior, the interior of another whale that swallowed it, and then the sea.
rows.anchor: وروي عن سالم بن أبي الجعد أنه قال: ظلمة جوف الحوت، ثم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the darknesses are the sea, the whale’s belly, and its intestines where Jonah was.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال: ظلمة البحر، وبطن الحوت ومعاؤها الذي كان فيه يونس

rows.speaker: محمد بن قيس
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Qays explains Jonah’s confession as admitting that he disobeyed God in what he did, while worshipping no one else.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن قيس (¬5): {إني كنت من الظالمين} حين عصيتك، وما صنعت

words: أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that none is deity except God and that He is exalted explains Jonah’s confession of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله: {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك}

words: أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet says that no Muslim who invokes with the prayer of Dhun-Nun in the whale is left unanswered; the source gives no grading.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، أن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال:

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret Jonah’s words as confession of sin and repentance, returning to God and reconsidering himself inside the whale.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتاده: هذا القول من يونس اعتراف بذنبه، وتوبة من خطيئة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses وعدا as an accusative verbal noun, since نعيده means “We promised this as a promise.”
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: منصوب على المصدر؛ لأن قوله: {نعيده} بمعنى وعدنا هذا وعدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the phrase means carrying out the very act itself; al-Zajjaj explains it as being able to do whatever God wills.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الفعل بعينه. ومعنى هذا ما ذكره الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpreters take the phrase to mean bringing creation into being and then restoring it: God will fulfill the promise of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون (¬3): يعني البدء والإعادة. والمعنى إنا كنا فاعلين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Said ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd take the Zabur as all revealed books and the Reminder as the heavenly Mother of the Book; Abu Ishaq agrees, and the author prefers this inclusive view.
rows.anchor: هذا قول سعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq includes the Torah, Gospel, and Quran among the books called Zabur; zabur and book share a sense, from the verb meaning to write.
rows.anchor: قال: الزبور جميع الكتب: التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in the reports of al-Kalbi, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi says the Reminder is the Torah and the Zabur means books revealed after it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي، والضحاك، والسدي: الذكر: التوراة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ata’s transmission, Ibn Abbas, and also Amir al-Sha‘bi, identify the Zabur as David’s Zabur and the Reminder as the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: يريد زبور داود من بعد التوراة. وهذا قول عامر الشعبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading is that God decreed and recorded His ruling in the books after the Mother of the Book.
rows.anchor: والمختار قول سعيد لأنه الأجمع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ata’s report, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu al-Aliya, Said ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd say the earth means Paradise; the righteous are believers who obey God, as supported by 39:74.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس -في رواية عطاء- ومجاهد والسدي، وأبو صالح، وأبو العالية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the earthly world will pass to this community’s believers, as God manifests the religion and conquers the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: يعني الدنيا تصير للمؤمنين من هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq parses ذلك as nominative, with an implied الأمر: the matter is thus.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: موضع (ذلك) رفع. المعنى: الأمر ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference is to the Hajj practices just mentioned.
rows.anchor: يعني ما ذكر من أعمال الحج.

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines a hurma as something whose violation is forbidden; a person may be respected because of companionship or a right.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: الحرمة ما لا يحل انتهاكه، وتقول: فلان له حرمة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a hurma as something one must uphold and may not neglect.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الحرمة: ما وجب القيام به وحرم التفريط فيه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the sacred limits here are God’s sins: prohibited things that must be left unviolated.
rows.anchor: فقال عطاء: هي معاصي الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid includes Mecca, Hajj, Umra, and sins forbidden by God; the author says this combines commanded rites, which must not be neglected, and forbidden acts, which must not be committed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الحرمة مكة والحج والعمرة، وما نهى الله عنه من معاصيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ata’s report says the phrase means God’s obligations and Sunna; the author prefers this as the most comprehensive account because it includes commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: يريد فرائض الله عز وجل وسننه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Many commentators, including Abu Ishaq, focus on pilgrimage, Umra, and the other rites, while allowing that every divine obligation is a sacred limit because neglect is forbidden.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو إسحاق: {حرمات الله}: الحج والعمرة وسائر المناسك. ثم قال: وكل ما فرضه الله

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba specifies stoning the pillars, standing at Muzdalifa, and similar rites; revering the rites means performing them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: يعني رمي (¬2) الجمار، والوقوف بجمع

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the sacred limits to five: the Sacred House, territory, month, mosque, and ihram; the author links this to 2:194.
rows.anchor: وخص ابن زيد الحرمات بما يقع عليه اسم الحرام، فقال: الحرمات: هي خمس: البيت الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun فهو refers to the act of revering; a verb can signify its verbal noun, which the pronoun then resumes.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {فهو} أي: التعظيم. والفعل يدل على المصدر، فكنى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being better for him with his Lord means reward in the afterlife; Ibn Abbas describes it as an increase in obedience and fear of God.
rows.anchor: وقوله {خير له عند ربه} يعني في الآخرة. وقال ابن عباس: فإن ذلك زيادة له في طاعة الله

words: وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permitted livestock are camels, cattle, and sheep, except the prohibitions recited in al-Maida, including carrion and animals strangled to death.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وأحلت لكم الأنعام} يعني: الإبل والبقر والغنم {إلا ما يتلى عليكم} أي: تحريمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means something foul or filthy, and every filthy thing is rijs; the discussion also appeared at 5:90 and 6:125.
rows.anchor: الرجس: الشيء القذر. وكل قذر رجس

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Shammar says Arabs called any erected figure of wood, stone, gold, silver, copper, or similar material a wathan; Christians also set up and venerated the cross.
rows.anchor: قال شمر: الأوثان عند العرب: كل تمثال من خشب أو حجارة أو ذهب أو فضة أو نحاس

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A‘sha calls the Christian cross a wathan in his poem, using the term for the object around which Christians worship.
rows.anchor: ولذلك سماه الأعشى وثنا، فقال:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In a report from Adi ibn Hatim, the Prophet calls the golden cross he wore a wathan and tells him to remove it; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وهو ما روي أن عدي بن حاتم قال: قدمت على النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wathan derives from the verb for standing firmly in place; wāthin means settled or stationary, and the poem describes keeping faith with old companions.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق هذا اللفظ من قولهم: وثن الشيء، إذا قام في مكانه وثبت. والواثن: الشيء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The command means to keep away from idols; Ibn Abbas glosses it specifically as avoiding their worship, which is rijs because it causes sin according to al-Kalbi.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: كونوا على جانب من الأوثان فإنها رجس. قال ابن عباس: يريد عبادة الأوثان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata’s report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd gloss rijs as punishment; al-Zajjaj says it is a curse in this world and punishment in the next.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: الرجس: العذاب

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ru’ba’s cited line uses الوثن for steadfastness in a bond; the author glosses it as remaining true to the old companionship.
rows.anchor: قال رؤبة: على أخلاء الصفاء الوثن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanations of rijs here repeat those given for 6:125.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأقوال ذكروها في قوله: {كذلك يجعل الله الرجس}

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes rijs as the consequence arising from idols, namely their worship; worship is called rijs because it leads to curse and punishment, or, for al-Kalbi, because it is sin.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش في هذه الآية: المعنى: فاجتنبوا الرجس الذي يكون منها

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq treats من as identifying a kind, so the sense is the rijs that is an idol; most exegetes take it as an explanatory مِن جنس.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (من) هاهنا تخليص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading rijs means the idol itself, called rijs as idol worship is called rijs in the other reading; it does not mean physical dirt or repulsiveness.
rows.anchor: وليس الرجس في هذه الآية من القذارة والاستقذار في شيء

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says all idols are rijs, so مِن associates the rijs with the noun rather than making it a part of the idols; he compares 48:29 and Sibawayh’s phrase about words of Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: {فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان} والأوثان كلها رجس، وتأويله -والله أعلم: فاجتنبوا الرجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zūr means falsehood and lying.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {واجتنبوا قول الزور} الزور (¬2): الباطل والكذب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Some identify the false statement as associating partners with God, including the pagan talbiya that made an idol a partner; Ata from Ibn Abbas says it was their claim that angels were God’s daughters.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد قولهم: الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Khuraym ibn Fatīk reports that the Prophet twice equated false testimony with associating partners, then recited this verse, pairing the bans on idol worship and false testimony.
rows.anchor: وروى خريم بن فاتك (¬6): أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قام خطيبا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The interpretation of false testimony as idolatrous speech is also attributed to Abdullah ibn Masud and Wa’il ibn Rabi‘a.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول عبد الله بن مسعود (¬2)، ووائل بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the verse also forbids inventing livestock taboos like those in 6:139 and the Bahira and Sa’iba; declaring something lawful or unlawful without warrant is lying against God.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق قولا آخر، فقال: الآية تدل على أنهم نهوا أن يحرموا

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says قد is a particle that affirms an occurrence, adding emphasis to the truth of the statement.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: (قد) حرف يوجب به الشيء

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians say قد can bring a past verb close to the present, as in قد قامت الصلاة.
rows.anchor: وقال النحويون (¬6): قد تقرب الماضي من الحال حتى تلحقه بحكمه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poem, أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج, likewise uses قد with a past form as a current state: crawling or toddling.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا قول الشاعر: أم صبي قد حبا أو دارج

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says a past verb used as a circumstantial clause requires قد, stated or understood, as in 4:90.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الحال (¬2) في الفعل الماضي لا يكون إلا بإضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here قد may emphasize the believers’ success or bring the past close to the present: their success has been attained and remains theirs now.
rows.anchor: و (قد) هاهنا يجوز أن تكون تأكيدا لفلاح المؤمنين، ويجوز أن تكون تقريبا للماضي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believers have attained felicity and remain in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: يريد قد سعد المصدقون وبقوا في الجنة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq explains their success as attaining everlasting life.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي قد نالوا البقاء الدائم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Humayd reports from Anas that the Prophet said God created and planted the Garden of Eden, told it to speak, and it said the believers had succeeded; the source gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وروى (¬3) حميد، عن أنس، أن رسول الله

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A report from Ka‘b likewise says God planted Eden with His hand and commanded it to speak, whereupon it declared the believers successful.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما يروى عن كعب أنه قال: إن الله غرس جنة عدن بيده

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri defines khushu in prayer as a person’s stillness; the Arabic root sense is stillness.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري (¬4): هو سكون المرء في صلاته

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the worshippers as humble; Mujahid and Ibrahim say still; Amr ibn Dinar says stillness and good bearing.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي: متواضعون (¬8). وقال مجاهد وإبراهيم: ساكنون (¬9). وقال عمرو بن دينار: هو السكون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret khushu as fear; the author says fear explains the stillness caused by fear of God rather than defining the word itself.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: خائفون (¬2). وهذا معنى؛ لأن (¬3) من سكن في صلاته إنما هو لخوفه من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the gaze and lowering oneself also express khushu, but both reduce to stillness.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك يؤول إلى السكون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the worshipper is so fearful of God that he does not know who is to his right or left.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما روي عن ابن عباس -في هذه الآية- قال: خشع

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that the Prophet used to look toward the sky during prayer until this verse came down; afterward he looked where he prostrated.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن سيرين قال: كان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- إذا صلى نظر في السماء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they give zakat from their wealth seeking God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يزكون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says they fulfill the obligatory charity.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: للصدقة الواجبة مؤدون

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq explains فاعلون as مؤتون, “giving.”
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معنى {فاعلون}: مؤتون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the trusts are deposits and other things entrusted to people.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أنها (¬2) أمانات الناس التي ائتمنوا عليها

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the trusts are obligations between God and a servant, hidden from others, such as ablution, ritual bathing, and fasting; most commentators prefer the people’s trusts.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنها أمانات بين الله وبين عبده مما لا يطلع عليه إلا الله، كالوضوء والغسل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the word in the singular, أمانتهم; a singular verbal noun or collective can denote many trusts.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير (لأمانتهم) واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular collective can include God-to-servant duties such as fasting, prayer, and washing, and human rights such as deposits and goods held in trust; أمانة is a verbal noun used for its object.
rows.anchor: والأمانة تختلف ولها ضروب نحو: الأمانة التي بين الله وبين عبده كالصيام والصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural is supported by 4:58; the author also compares the singular collective at 6:108 with the plural أعمال at 23:63.
rows.anchor: ووجه الجمع قوله تعالى: {إن الله يأمركم أن تؤدوا الأمانات إلى أهلها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أمانة is a verbal noun used to name the thing entrusted.
rows.anchor: والأمانة مصدر سمي به المفعول.

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says their عهد means the oaths taken from them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يقول وحلفهم الذي يؤخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes عهد as contracts they made with other people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني العقود التي عاقدوا الناس عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: راعي means keeping or guarding.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {راعون} حافظون.

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says the root of ra‘y is taking responsibility to maintain and put right what is entrusted to one, whether a ruler’s subjects, a shepherd’s flock, or relations with another person.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أصل الرعي (¬2) في اللغة: القيام على إصلاح

words: ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new generation is Aad, the people of Hud, and the messenger sent among them is Hud.
rows.anchor: يعني عادا قوم هود، [وأراد

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The repeated أن has one sense, and the separation by إذا makes the repetition sound well-formed; Abdullah’s reading has only one أن after إذا.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أعيدت (أنكم) مرتين ومعناهما واحد، إلا أن ذلك حسن لما فرق بينهما بإذا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq parses the first أنكم as an object of promise, conventionally with an understood ب; some treat the second أن as occupying the same position and repeated for emphasis, yielding the sense that resurrection follows death. He compares 9:63.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: {أنكم} موضعها نصب على معنى: أيعدكم بأنكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali lists analyses of the second أن: apposition, emphasis, an uncounted extra particle, or being raised by the adverb. Sibawayh chooses apposition, Abu al-Abbas and al-Jarmi emphasis, and Abu al-Hasan the adverbial analysis; no one endorses the extra-particle view.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: لا يخلو (أن) الثانية في قوله: {أيعدكم أنكم} الآية

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the second أن as replacing the first: the intended sense is that you will be brought out when you die, with the first particle placed early to signal what precedes resurrection.
rows.anchor: فمذهب (¬7) سيبويه (¬8): أن الثانية بدل من الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan says the second أن is raised by the adverbial phrase.
rows.anchor: ومذهب أبي الحسن (¬10) أنه مرتفع بالظرف

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali notes that no one considered the second particle an extra element to be disregarded.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أحد أنه زائد غير معتد به

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects Sibawayh’s apposition analysis: the first أن is not complete before إذا متم, and that time clause cannot be a predicate of the addressed persons; the parallel conditional in 9:63 also cannot complete the first clause.
rows.anchor: قال أبو على: لا يجوز عندي (¬4) أن تكون (أن) الثانية

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Abbas calls repetition of the second أن the best account, since it means the same as the first; Abu Ali says even this fails because the particle cannot be repeated without its clause.
rows.anchor: وأبو العباس يذهب إلى أن الثانية مكررة توكيدا، ولست تريد بها إلا ما أردت بالأولى. قال (¬5): وهذا أحسن الأقاويل عندي في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects Abu al-Abbas’s emphasis analysis: one cannot repeat أن alone without its clause, and the first clause has not completed its complement; he says it remains closer than apposition.
rows.anchor: فلا يجوز التكرير (¬8) فيها وحدها، كما لا تكرر سائر الموصولات دون

words: أَنَّكُم إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنتُمْ تُرَابًۭا وَعِظَٰمًا أَنَّكُم مُّخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali concludes that the second أن is raised by the overt ظرف إذا: the clause from إذا متم through مخرجون serves as the first أن’s predicate, with the sense that resurrection is at the time of death.
rows.anchor: ثبت أنها مرتفعة بالظرف الظاهر الذي هو (إذا)

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Those who defend apposition may posit an omitted إخراجكم, making extraction at death a complete predicate; a time phrase can predicate an event, unlike the persons addressed. Those who defend repetition need no omitted word.
rows.anchor: من قدر [في] (¬12) (أن) الثانية البدل فإنه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali argues وعد takes two direct objects, so the first أنكم can be accusative as the second object without an implied ب, as Quranic usage shows at 48:20, 20:80, 7:142, 48:29, and 9:114.
rows.anchor: قال: فأما (¬4) قول أبي إسحاق {أيعدكم أنكم} إن موضع (أن) الأولى نصب

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: The Quranic examples show وعد takes its second object without a preposition, so no حرف الخفض need be supplied in this verse.
rows.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تقدير الباء ألا ترى أن ما جاء في التنزيل من هذا بغير الباء
